prompt: For answering from weekly-changing internal documentation, RAG beats fine-tuning primarily because…

options.text: …retrieval reads current documents at question time, while fine-tuning bakes a stale snapshot into weights: uncitable and permission-blind

explanation: Knowledge that changes belongs outside the weights: update the index, not the model, and get citations and per-user access control as side benefits.

prompt: A RAG assistant answers wrongly; inspection shows the retrieved chunks were about the wrong product edition. The bug lives in…

options.text: …retrieval: the generator faithfully used wrong context; a bigger model would just phrase the same error better

explanation: Garbage in, eloquent garbage out. Stage-localized debugging (retrieve vs. generate) is the core RAG skill.

prompt: The fundamental chunking trade-off is…

options.text: …small chunks match specifically but may lack surrounding context; large chunks carry context but dilute relevance scoring
…there is no trade-off; smaller is always better

explanation: Specific-but-insufficient vs. sufficient-but-blurry. Structural chunking (clauses, sections) with slight overlap is the practical resolution.

prompt: Queries containing exact error codes retrieve poorly under pure semantic search because…

options.text: …embeddings blur exact identifiers into general meaning-space: hybrid retrieval adds BM25 keyword matching to restore exactness
…the codes are too recent to be indexed

explanation: Semantic and keyword search fail in complementary ways: paraphrase vs. identifiers. Running both and merging is the default production architecture.

prompt: What does a reranker add on top of embedding-based retrieval?

options.text: It scores query-chunk pairs jointly with a model, ordering the top candidates far more accurately than raw vector distance
It compresses chunks to save tokens
It replaces the need for embeddings entirely

explanation: Embedding search is a fast wide net; the reranker is a careful judge over the top ~20, keeping the best 3–5 for the prompt.

prompt: Why must a RAG system have an explicit, exactly-phrased abstention response?

options.text: Models may still answer when evidence is missing; a defined abstention policy, measurable response, and routing path make insufficient evidence an explicit outcome
It makes the bot sound humble

explanation: Abstention is engineered, not emergent, and the exact phrasing makes it detectable, so evals can measure abstention rate on unanswerable questions.

prompt: Recall@5 answers which question?

options.text: Was at least one truly relevant chunk among the top 5 retrieved?
Did the model answer in under 5 seconds?

explanation: Recall@k measures whether generation ever had a chance. If the relevant chunk isn't in the top k, no downstream fix can help.

prompt: End-to-end quality is 71%; retrieval recall@5 is 62%. The right next investment is…

options.text: …retrieval improvements (chunking, hybrid weights, reranking): recall caps everything downstream

explanation: In ~38% of cases the generator never saw the answer. Raise the ceiling first; tune generation second. This is why the stages are evaluated separately.

prompt: Why do RAG eval sets deliberately include unanswerable questions?

options.text: The abstention rate on them is the hallucination alarm: a system that answers everything is fabricating on schedule
Unanswerable questions should never be in evals

explanation: Correct behavior on 'no answer exists' is refusal. Measuring it requires questions where refusal is the right answer.

prompt: Which metadata should chunks carry at ingestion? Select all that apply.

options.text: A copy of every other chunk for context

explanation: Citations, freshness filtering, and permission-aware retrieval all depend on metadata attached at ingestion. Duplicating the corpus into each chunk defeats chunking.

prompt: Per-user document permissions in RAG are enforced correctly by…

options.text: …filtering at retrieval time so unauthorized chunks never enter the context
…asking the model politely not to reveal restricted content it was given

explanation: Anything in context can come out of the model: instructions are not a security boundary (Module 15 doubles down on this). Access control happens before the prompt is built.

prompt: Why are per-claim citations more than a UX nicety?

options.text: They make every claim checkable: by users, reviewers, and automated faithfulness evals; an uncitable claim is a fabrication flag
They increase answer length, which improves quality
They are required by all embedding models

explanation: Verifiability is the product. Citations turn 'trust me' into 'check me', and give your evaluation pipeline a hook to grade faithfulness automatically.

prompt: Chunk overlap (repeating a sentence or two between adjacent chunks) exists to…

options.text: …keep answers that span a chunk boundary retrievable, without overlap, a fact split across the cut may match neither chunk well

explanation: Boundaries are arbitrary; meaning isn't. Modest overlap insures against the cut landing mid-answer, at a small storage cost.

prompt: Adding a reranker improved answer quality but added 300ms. The correct evaluation frame is…

options.text: …measure both: retrieval-metric gain (recall/MRR) and p95 latency cost, then decide against your latency budget: quality changes are never free-standing
…use the vendor's aggregate benchmark without measuring your workload

explanation: Every pipeline stage buys something and costs something. The budgets (Module 16) and the evals (Module 14) jointly make the call, not either alone.

prompt: Why is the abstention response given an exact, fixed phrasing rather than letting the model improvise a refusal?

options.text: Exact phrasing is detectable (by evals measuring abstention rates, by routing logic, and by UX) while improvised refusals are unmeasurable and unroutable
A fixed response improves the model's underlying factual knowledge
Variable refusals cannot be displayed in a user interface

explanation: Abstention is an engineered, instrumented behavior. If you can't detect it, you can't measure it; if you can't measure it, you can't maintain it.

prompt: Retrieval evals report recall@5 = 95% but users still get wrong answers on recently-changed policies. The likely culprit is…

options.text: …index staleness: retrieval correctly finds chunks from outdated documents; freshness through change detection, upserts, and deletion propagation is a separate quality axis

explanation: An index is a derived cache of sources. Recall measures finding what's indexed, not whether what's indexed still reflects reality. Both need monitoring.

prompt: Deleting a document from the source system must trigger…

options.text: …deletion of its chunks from the index (via stable chunk IDs): otherwise the assistant confidently cites retracted content indefinitely

explanation: Deletion propagation is the forgotten half of ingestion, and the compliance-relevant half, when the deleted document was retracted for a reason.

prompt: In a multi-tenant RAG product, per-tenant isolation belongs…

options.text: …in the data layer: separate collections or provably mandatory tenant filters, making a cross-tenant query impossible rather than merely avoided
…in the system prompt ('only discuss this tenant's documents')

explanation: One forgotten filter on a shared index is a cross-customer breach. Structure beats vigilance: make the wrong query unexpressible.

prompt: Upgrading the embedding model requires re-embedding the whole corpus because…

options.text: …different models define different vector spaces: similarity between old and new vectors is meaningless, so mixed indexes silently break retrieval

explanation: Each model's geometry is its own ruler. Operationally: build the new index fully, verify recall on evals, blue/green swap with rollback ready.

prompt: The metric 'time since last successful ingestion per source' with an alert threshold exists to catch…

options.text: …silent pipeline death: the most common way RAG rots: nothing errors user-visibly, the index just quietly stops reflecting reality

explanation: Staleness is invisible at query time: answers keep flowing, just increasingly wrong. A freshness metric makes the invisible failure page someone.
